rationale: OilAlpha is a mobile-focused actor; detecting its application-layer C2 identifies beaconing from compromised (potentially BYOD) devices, evidencing that mobile-device threat monitoring is implemented and can trigger containment/remote wipe. NIST anchors sit in the SC-* family (SC-07/SC-10/SC-20-23), aligned with 2-6's mobile-communications protection intent.

rationale: Both Domestic Kitten and OilAlpha deliver malicious mobile apps/files that users are lured into installing. Hunting for this malicious-file execution directly evidences the 2-6-3 intent around controlled use of mobile devices and user awareness against rogue apps; detection reduces real mobile-compromise risk.

rationale: Camera/video surveillance is a signature capability of these mobile surveillanceware actors. rationale: Detecting bulk collection of data from the local system evidences monitoring of unauthorized access to protected/classified data (the confidentiality outcome of 2-7). NIST anchors include SC-28 (data at rest), SC-13, AC-16 and AC-23, which align to data-and-information protection; detection surfaces theft-in-progress but does not itself implement classification/labeling.

rationale: Inhibit System Recovery (e.g. deleting volume shadow copies/backup catalogs) is the one destructive technique that directly attacks the recovery mechanism 2-9 protects. Early detection can stop backup destruction before recoverability is lost, so it genuinely reduces risk. NIST anchors CP-09 (backup) and CP-10 (recovery) align tightly with the subdomain.

rationale: Data destruction detection alerts to a recovery-triggering event, and CTID anchors it to CP-09/CP-10, but detecting destruction does not itself provide or test backups. 2-9's protective value is having recoverable, tested backups; detection is nominal against that intent, so the flag is false despite the strong-looking control-family match.

rationale: Ransomware encryption for impact is the classic driver for restore-from-backup. CTID anchors it to CP-09/CP-10, but detecting encryption does not evidence that backups exist or that restore has been tested (2-9-3). The mapping is nominal for the backup control: the control is satisfied by tested backups, not by ransomware detection.
